prompt_en: Photograph a Clockpunk environment with a reference-guided human subject, caught during a visible clockwork event in a sun-struck civic reading court. The central fictional woman is the keeper of its shade canopy. Use the supplied portrait as visible face and hair guidance: a soft oval face, large dark-brown eyes, a straight nose and softly defined pink lips; a dark jaw-length bob with a lightly separated fringe. Her ink-blue square-neck linen dress and warm reflected light give her a quiet, attractive presence while her attention stays on the work. She stands beside a waist-high handwheel at the open edge of a limestone loggia, her torso angled comfortably toward it. Her right hand grips the upper rim and her left hand steadies the lower rim, both elbows bent with room beside her body. Her shoulders are relaxed and her head turns slightly toward the camera side as she looks up to check the nearest louver, keeping both eyes readable. The wheel's horizontal spindle enters a small brass pinion visibly meshed with a larger toothed wheel in an open iron frame. A crank arm on that larger wheel connects to a slender vertical rod; the rod rises in clear view to a short tie-bar attached to the pivot arms of the overhead louver bank. Broad oak slats with bronze edges sit partly tilted, their common pivots and connecting bar easy to distinguish. Worn contact surfaces and fresh polished arcs on the gear teeth suggest a mechanism used every day. The present adjustment has just brought the first broad band of shade across a stone reading table. One of two waiting readers slides an open book into that cool band: the open volume rests on the stone tabletop, with the reader's fingertips against its lower edge at the shade boundary. The other reader still shades their eyes in the adjacent sun. The keeper watches the slat rather than performing for the camera; the readers' small responses make her effort matter. Warm limestone, dark timber and restrained brass hold the palette together. Make an inhabited environmental photograph from the open side of the loggia at the keeper's chest height, in a horizontal 4:3 frame with natural 35 mm perspective. Frame her from mid-thigh upward, placing her face and handwheel prominently in the foreground and the complete short drive linkage along the right side. Include the low canopy above and the table behind within the same readable depth. Crisp noon light makes the moving shade boundary graphic; soft reflected stone light retains the reference face's form and the hands' contact. Preserve enough depth of field to read the gear mesh, linkage endpoints and readers together, with tactile photographic skin, linen, timber and metal.
